la:adj:blandus.html:
blandus, a, um, adj.
for mlandus; akin to μείλιχος, mollis, mulier; Goth. milds; Engl. mild
,
of a smooth tongue, flattering, fawning, caressing (class and very freq.).
Lit.: blanda es parum,: nemini credo qui large blandu'st dives pauperi,: ut unus omnium homo te vivat numquam quisquam blandior,: scis me minime esse blandum,: unum te puto minus blandum esse quam me,: blandum amicum a vero secernere,: (Alcibiades) affabilis, blandus, temporibus callidissime inserviens,: an blandiores (mulieres) in publico quam in privato et alienis quam vestris estis?: tum neque subjectus solito nec blandior esto,: canes,: catulorum blanda propago,; ; : columba,: tigres,; ; ; —
Poet. constr.
With gen.: precum,.—
With acc.: genas vocemque,.—
With inf.: blandum et auritas fidibus canoris Ducere quercus,; . —
With abl.: chorus implorat. .doctā prece blandus ( = blande supplicans dis carmine quod poëta eum docuit. Orell. ad loc.),.—
Trop. (mostly of things).
Flattering, pleasant, agreeable, enticing, alluring, charming, seductive (cf. blandior, II. B.; blanditia, II.): blandā voce vocare, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 51 Vahl.): ne blandā aut supplici oratione fallamur,; : voces,; : preces,; ; ; : querelae,: laudes,: verba,; : dicta,; 9, 156: os,: pectus, Afran. ap. .—So, voluptas, ; ; ; 5, 179; : amor,; : Veneris blandis sub armis,amaracini liquor,: tura,: manus,; cf. : aquae,: caudae, al.: otium consuetudine in dies blandius,: blandiores suci,; : blandissima litora, Baiae,; : actio,: ministerium, Cod. Th. 10, 10, 12, § 1.— With dat.: et blandae superūm mortalibus irae,: neque admittunt orationes sermonesve... jucunda dictu aut legentibus blanda,.—
Of persons: filiolus,; cf.: nam et voluptates, blandissimae dominae (the most alluring mistresses), majores partes animi a virtute detorquent, .—
Persuading by caressing, persuasive: nunc experiemur, nostrum uter sit blandior,. —Hence, adv., in three forms, soothingly, flatteringly, courteously, etc.
Anteclass. form blandĭter, ; ; Titin. ap. (also p. 256, 15), and ap. P.—
Class. form blandē, : compellare hominem,: me adpellare,: adloqui,: dicere,; cf.: blande, leniter, dulciter dicere,; and blande ac benedice,: rogare,: excepti hospitio ab Tullo blande ac benigne,: quaerere,: linguā lambere,: et satiati agni ludunt blandeque coruscant,: colere fructus,to treat carefully, gently, (cf. blandimentum, II. B.): flectere cardinem sonantem,softly, carefully,—Comp.: blandius petere,: ad aurem invocabat, Cael. ap. : moderere fidem,—Sup.: blandissime appellat hominem,.—*
blandum = blande: ridere,.

la:verb:blandio.html:
blandĭo, īre, 4 (
act. collat. form of blandior), to caress, coax, court: cur ego blandirem (mulierem),—Part. pass.: blanditusque labor molli curabitur arte, Verr. ap. P.: blandiendo duce nutrivit malum,.

la:verb:blandior.html:
blandĭor, ītus, 4, v. dep.
blandus
.
Prop., lit., to cling caressingly to one, to fawn upon, to flatter, soothe, caress, fondle, coax (class.).
With dat.: matri interfectae infante miserabiliter blandiente,.—
With inter se, .—
With ut and subj.: Hannibalem pueriliter blandientem patri ut duceretur in Hispaniam,.—
Absol.: cessit immanis tibi blandienti Janitor aulae Cerberus,: tantusque in eo vigor, et dulcis quidam blandientis risus apparuit, ut, etc.,: et modo blanditur, modo... Terret,.—
Transf.
In gen., to flatter, make flattering, courteous speeches, be complaisant to.
With dat.: nostro ordini palam blandiuntur,: blandiri eis subtiliter a quibus est petendum,: cur matri praeterea blanditur?: durae supplex blandire puellae,: sic (Venus) patruo blandita suo est,; ; .—
Absol.: quippe qui litigare se simulans blandiatur,: lingua juvet, mentemque tegat. Blandire, noceque,: in blandiendo (vox) lenis et summissa,: pavidum blandita,timidly coaxing,: qui cum dolet blanditur, post tempus sapit, Publ. Syr. v. 506 Rib.—
With per: de Commageno mirifice mihi et per se et per Pomponium blanditur Appius, (12), 2.—
With abl.: torrenti ac meditatā cotidie oratione blandiens,.—
In partic.
Blandiri sibi, etc., to flatter one's self with something, to fancy something, delude one's self: blandiuntur enim sibi, qui putant, etc.,.—So often in Dig. et Codd.; cf.: ne nobis blandiar,not to flatter ourselves, to tell the whole truth,.—
Pregn., to persuade or impel by flattery ( = blandiendo persuadeo or compello—very rare).
With subj.: (ipsa voluptas) res per Veneris blanditur saecla propagent ( = sic blanditur ut propagent), Lachm.—
With ab and ad: cum etiam saepe blandiatur gratia conviviorum a veris indiciis ad falsam probationem,—
Trop.
Of inanim. things as subjects, to flatter, please, be agreeable or favorable to; to allure by pleasure, to attract, entice, invite.
With dat.: video quam suaviter voluptas sensibus nostris blandiatur,: blandiebatur coeptis fortuna,. —
Absol.: fortuna cum blanditur captatum venit, Publ. Syr. v. 167 Rib: blandiente inertiā,: ignoscere vitiis blandientibus,; ; .—
With abl.: opportuna suā blanditur populus umbrā, Ov M. 10, 555.—
Of things as objects: cur ego non votis blandiar ipse meis?i. e. believe what I wish,: nisi tamen auribus nostris bibliopolae blandiuntur,tickle with flattery,.—Hence,
Subst.: blandĭens, entis, m., a flatterer: adversus blandientes incorruptus,.—
blandītus, a, um, P. a., pleasant, agreeable, charming (rare): rosae,peregrinatio,.

blasphēmo, āre,
v. a., = βλασφημέω (eccl. Lat.), to revile, reproach, ; God and divine things, to blaspheme: Christum,: nomen Domini,; ; . 3; 26, 65.

la:noun:blandimentum.html:
blandīmentum, i, n.
blandior
.
flattering words, blandishment, complimentary speech, flattery (class.; most freq. in plur. and in Tac.): nec eam (virtutem) minis aut blandimentis corrupta deseret,: pessum dedisti me blandimentis tuis,; : multa igitur blandimenta plebi per id tempus ab senatu data,: captus blandimentis,: per blandimenta juvenem aggredi,; : muliebribus blandimentis infectae epistulae,.—In sing., .—And in poet. exuberance: cui blandimenta precesque Verbaque jactanti mitissima, desine, dixit, etc.,.—
Trop.
Any thing that pleases the senses, an object that charms, an allurement, a pleasure, charm, delight: multa nobis blandimenta natura ipsa genuit,: blandimenta vitae

= res, quae vitam jucundam reddunt), ; (cf.: delinimenta vitae,): aestivi caloris,: vecturae,.—Of the spices, seasoning, condiments in food, ; .—

Healing applications, cures: alia quoque blandimenta excogitabat,.—
Careful culture: hoc blandimento (i. e. blanda cultura) impetratis radicibus,.

la:noun:blasphemia.html:
blasphēmĭa, ae, f. (blasphēmĭ-um, ii, n., ), = βλασφημία (eccl. Lat.),
a reviling, slander, ; towards God,blasphemy,, n. 2; ; ; ; ; .

la:noun:blanditia.html:
blandĭtĭa, ae (blandĭtĭes, ēi, in abl., ), f.
blandus
.
The quality of one blandus; a caressing, flattering, flattery (mostly in an honorable sense; cf. on the contrary, assentatio and adulatio; class in prose and poetry; most freq. in plur.).
Sing.: haec meretrix meum erum blanditiā intulit in pauperiem,: viscus merus vostra'st blanditia,: in cive excelso atque homine nobili blanditiam, ostentationem, ambitionem notam esse levitatis, (ap. ): nullam in amicitiā pestem esse majorem quam adulationem, blanditiam, adsentationem,: occursatio et blanditia popularis,; cf. ; —
Plur., flatteries, blandishments, allurements, = blandimenta: puerique parentum blanditiis facile ingenium fregere superbum, caresses, * ; : quot illic (sc. in amore) blanditiae, quot illic iracundiae sunt!: ut blanditiis suis suam voluptatem expleat,: quam (benevolentiam civium) blanditiis et adsentando conligere turpe est,: tantum apud te ejus blanditiae flagitiosae voluerunt, ut, etc.,: hereditates... malitiosis blanditiis quaesitae,; : blanditiis ab aliquo aliquid exprimere,: muliebres,: virorum factum purgantium,: fallaces,: verniles,; ; cf. also ; ; ; 1, 9, 77; ; ; ; ; ; 6, 632; 6, 685; 7, 817; 10, 259; 12, 407; 14, 19; ; .—
Trop., pleasure, delight, enticement, charm, allurement (cf. blandus, II. A., and blandior, II. B.): blanditiis praesentium voluptatum deliniti atque corrupti,: attrita cotidiano actu forensi ingenia optime rerum talium blanditia (i. e. lectione poëtarum) reparantur. .

an insect that shuns the light; of several kinds, the cockroach, chafer, moth, etc., ; : lucifuga, (per noctem vagans, Serv.); cf. ; ; ; ; cf. Voss, Verg. l. l.—On account of its mean appearance: amore cecidi tamquam blatta in pelvim, Laber. ap. .
